content.text:
I fixed it: two equal `OrderedSet`s now get the same `hashCode()` no matter how they were built. I reproduced the bug before the fix, the case now passes, and the full test suite passes (683 passed, 1 skipped).

**Cause:** an `OrderedSet` stores its items in an `OrderedMap`, which keeps them in an internal list. When you remove an item, it usually leaves an empty slot in that list instead of shifting everything down. `OrderedMap.__iterate` reported how many slots it walked over, empty ones included. `hashCode()` uses that number as the size, so a set that had items removed hashed differently from an identical set built directly. For example, `OrderedSet(['d','a','b','c']).remove('d')` vs `OrderedSet(['a','b','c'])`.

**Fix:** in `src/OrderedMap.js`, `__iterate` now counts only real entries. The same change applies to `OrderedMap` itself, since it had the same problem.

`is()` already returned `true` for my repro sets before the change; only the hash was different. I couldn't open the jsfiddle, so I can't confirm the screenshot shows the same case. If that example also had `equals()` returning `false`, it's worth checking it against this build. I didn't add a regression test.
